title: Minor and major upgrades: in-place, dump and restore, logical replication

videos.script: Every PostgreSQL server you look after will be upgraded, and there are two kinds of upgrade. {{two}} A minor one moves from 16.2 to 16.15. The files on disk stay exactly as they are. You replace the programs and restart, and the database is down for a few seconds. {{minor}} A major one moves from 16 to 17, and that is a different job. Version 17 cannot read the catalogue 16 wrote, so something has to carry your data across. {{major}} There are three ways to carry it. pg_upgrade rewrites the catalogue and keeps the data files, so it takes seconds. A dump and restore copies everything as SQL, so it takes as long as the data is big. Logical replication keeps a new server in step with the old one, so the switch itself is almost instant. {{three}} None of them should run for the first time on the server people depend on. So this lesson upgrades a copy. You will make a rehearsal cluster, watch an upgrade refuse, fix why, and run it again. {{rehearsal}} At the end your own server is still on 16, untouched, and you know what the real night will look like. {{title}}
